chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a group of people upon whom a roof fell; how is their inheritance? He said: 'Some of them inherit from others.'

key_terms.يُورَثُ: he is inherited from / he inherits

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed among people who die simultaneously in the same accident?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the inheritance dynamics for a group perishing simultaneously, such as under a collapsed roof, by ruling that they inherit from one another. This establishes the principle of concurrent death (*al-mutawaffun bi-waqtin wahid*) where the estate circulates among the deceased before final distribution to their respective heirs, avoiding the complexity of determining precise chronological order of death. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for handling mass casualty inheritance cases where the sequence of death is unknown.
